title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2% above regular)
drivers.evidence: Past weeks with price increase (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) show median x0.9 vs baseline; noise-adjusted price effect shrunk to x0.9.

drivers.name: TikTok trend (novel driver)
drivers.evidence: No prior occurrence; only one past social media trend; noise-adjusted estimate shrunk toward 1.0. Plausible but uncertain upside.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.6. No events are scheduled. The price is 6.2% above regular, which typically suppresses demand—past promotions show price increases reduce sales. The product is trending on TikTok, a novel driver with no prior data. The classical uplift model gives 1.00, but this ignores the price hike and untested social media effect. Recent weeks show no clear trend. The TikTok trend is uncertain (one occurrence), so shrink its effect. Price increase of +6.2% suggests downside. Use noise-adjusted effect for price: prior price hikes (e.g., 2026-09-28) show ~x0.9. Combine: x0.9 (price) × x1.1 (TikTok, shrunk) ≈ x1.0. Final median multiplier near 1.0. Spreads unchanged—no strong evidence for volatility shift.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Product is trending on TikTok

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.6 | 5%-95%: 2.9 - 39.3 | 10%-90%: 6.9 - 34.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
